verses.text: David built houses for himself in David's City. He prepared a place for God's ark and set up a tent for it.
Then David said, “Only the Levites should carry God's ark. The LORD chose them to carry it and serve him forever.”
David gathered all Israel in Jerusalem to bring the LORD's ark to the place he had prepared for it.
David assembled Aaron's descendants and the Levites:
from Kohath's descendants, Uriel their leader and a hundred and twenty of his relatives;
from Merari's descendants, Asaiah their leader and two hundred and twenty of his relatives;
from Gershom's descendants, Joel their leader and a hundred and thirty of his relatives;
from Elizaphan's descendants, Shemaiah their leader and two hundred of his relatives;
from Hebron's descendants, Eliel their leader and eighty of his relatives;
and from Uzziel's descendants, Amminadab their leader and a hundred and twelve of his relatives.
David summoned Zadok and Abiathar the priests and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.

He told them, “You're the heads of the Levite families. Set yourselves and your relatives apart for this work, so you can bring the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place I've prepared for it.
The LORD our God broke out against us in anger because you didn't carry it the first time. We hadn't asked him how to do it according to his instructions.”
So the priests and Levites consecrated themselves to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.
The Levites carried God's ark on their shoulders with its poles, as Moses had commanded in keeping with the LORD's word.
David told the Levite leaders to appoint some of their relatives as singers and musicians. They were to play stringed instruments, harps, and cymbals and lift their voices loudly with joy.
The Levites appointed Heman son of Joel, his relative Asaph son of Berechiah, and Ethan son of Kushaiah from their relatives in Merari's family.

With them came their relatives of the second rank: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, and the gatekeepers Obed-Edom and Jeiel.
The singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were assigned to sound the bronze cymbals.
Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah played stringed instruments set to Alamoth.
Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah led with harps tuned to the eight-stringed lyre.
Chenaniah, a Levite leader, was in charge of the singing. He taught the singers because he was skilled.
Berechiah and Elkanah guarded the ark.
The priests Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer blew trumpets ahead of God's ark. Obed-Edom and Jehiah guarded the ark.
David, Israel's elders, and the commanders of thousands went joyfully to bring the ark of the LORD's covenant up from Obed-Edom's house.
Because God helped the Levites who carried the ark of the LORD's covenant, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
David wore a robe of fine linen, as did all the Levites who carried the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah, who led the singers. David also wore a linen ephod.
All Israel brought up the ark of the LORD's covenant with shouts, horns, trumpets, cymbals, and the loud music of stringed instruments and harps.
As the ark of the LORD's covenant entered David's City, Saul's daughter Michal looked out the window. She saw King David dancing and celebrating and felt contempt for him.
